stories.headline: Cascador and Sterling Bank Debut $200 Million Startup Loan Facility
stories.dek: The massive new fund aims to derisk traditional bank financing for growing Nigerian technology enterprises.
stories.body:
Accessing traditional bank financing has long been a major hurdle for tech ventures operating across Nigeria. To bridge this funding gap, Cascador and Sterling Bank have teamed up to launch a substantial $200 million fund designed to make borrowing easier for local startups.

Reported by TechCabal, the initiative tackles the core issue of default risk by sharing the burden between the institutions. By helping to derisk these loans, the program encourages traditional lenders to open their doors wider to emerging companies.

Securing debt financing has historically proven difficult because lenders often view early-stage ventures as volatile or high-risk investments. This new partnership aims to shift that dynamic by building a safety net that protects lenders while giving founders the liquidity needed to scale operations.

The arrival of the $200 million pool represents a notable shift in how financial institutions engage with the startup ecosystem. By blending risk-sharing mechanisms with substantial capital, the fund could pave the way for more predictable avenues of business growth.
